configurePresets.name: release
configurePresets.description: The everyday configuration: optimized build for ctest and main_norm. NOTE the build type is set explicitly. An empty CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE compiles the C++ reference and the bandwidth probes at -O0 while leaving the .S kernels unaffected — the Sprint-5 defect that made single-core NEON read 10.8 GiB/s against SSVE's 59.4, i.e. a benchmark comparing an unoptimized C++ probe against optimized assembly.

configurePresets.name: debug
configurePresets.description: Address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers for correctness work. CLAUDE.md §7 calls for sanitizer runs when a layout bug is suspected; this makes that a one-liner rather than hand-edited flags. NOT for timing: the instrumentation makes every GiB/s figure meaningless.

configurePresets.name: release-submission
configurePresets.displayName: release-submission — the exact configuration behind the reported numbers
configurePresets.description: Settings identical to `release`, kept as a separately named preset so the configuration behind the submitted benchmark tables is a named artifact rather than a command someone has to remember. Built into its own directory so a submission run cannot pick up stale objects from day-to-day work. main_norm prints git SHA, build type, compiler, OS and detected SME/SME2 features, so a run from this preset is self-describing and can be checked against the report.
